message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Create a GitHub Pages static homepage + port 8253 Node.js backend blog server
   - The blog must simultaneously serve TWO purposes:
     1. External promotion of FreeLang technology achievements (showcasing excellence)
     2. Official technical verification report documenting deficiencies and incomplete features
   - Implement a full comment system with write, read, delete, and search functionality via API
   - Serve 89 technical blog posts across both promotional and verification categories

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Dual-architecture: GitHub Pages (static frontend) + Node.js backend (dynamic API)
   - CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) for cross-domain API calls
   - Fetch API for asynchronous HTTP communication
   - Markdown-to-HTML conversion via regex patterns
   - File-based JSON persistence (comments.json)
   - RESTful API design for CRUD operations
   - Binary categorization of blog posts (promotional vs verification)
   - Query string filtering and searching

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - projects/fl-blog/index.html (GitHub Pages static homepage):
     - Two-column layout with "우리 기술 (External Promotion)" and "기술 검증 (Technical Verification)"
     - Stats display (89 posts, 50K+ words, 100+ code examples)
     - Official verification table with status indicators:
       - ✅ Complete: Compiler (Lexer→Parser→AST), Database (Zero-Copy, MVCC)
       - ⚠️ Needs Improvement: Markdown (basic features, no tables/footnotes)
       - ❌ Not Implemented: Search, Comments
     - Filter tabs: "전체 (89)" / "우리 기술 홍보" / "기술 검증"
     - JavaScript: dynamically fetches posts from backend, filters by category, displays with badges
     - fetch('http://localhost:8253/api/posts') integration

   - projects/fl-blog/server.js (Original Node.js backend):
     - HTTP server on port 8253
     - GET / - serves index.html
     - GET /api/posts - returns JSON array of all 89 posts
     - GET /post/{slug} - renders individual post with Markdown→HTML conversion
     - GET /health - JSON health check
     - Loads posts from posts/ directory, parses YAML frontmatter, generates slugs

   - projects/fl-blog/server-comments.js (NEW: Extended backend with comments):
     - All endpoints from server.js PLUS:
     - GET /api/comments?postId={slug} - retrieves all comments for a post, sorted newest first
     - POST /api/comments - creates new comment with JSON body: {postSlug, author, email, text}
       - Validates required fields (postSlug, author, text)
       - Stores with timestamp and unique ID
       - Returns created comment object
     - DELETE /api/comments/{id} - removes comment by ID
     - GET /api/search?q={query} - searches comments by full-text match on text/author fields
     - Comments persisted to comments.json via saveComments() function
     - Enhanced POST /post/{slug} response includes:
       - Comment count in header
       - Comment form with author/email/text fields (JavaScript: submitComment/deleteComment functions)
       - Comment list with author name, date, text, delete link
       - Uses Highlight.js for syntax highlighting
     - All endpoints return proper HTTP status codes and JSON responses

   - projects/fl-blog/posts/ directory:
     - 89 markdown files in format: 2026-03-27-filename.md
     - Examples: 2026-03-28-Phase1-001-ZeroCopy-Database.md, 2026-03-28-Phase4-045-Stream-Processing.md
     - Each file contains YAML frontmatter (title, date) and markdown body
     - Dynamically categorized: first ~35 posts = "promo", remaining ~54 = "tech" (based on Phase numbers)

   - projects/fl-blog/main.go (Go backend - working but Termux incompatible):
     - internal/post/post.go: Post struct, LoadPosts(), parsePost(), slug extraction, excerpt generation
     - internal/render/markdown.go: ToHTML() function converting markdown to HTML
     - internal/tmpl/tmpl.go: RenderIndex(), RenderPost(), RenderJSON() template functions
     - 796 total lines of code, zero external dependencies (stdlib only)
     - Compiled to 8.2MB binary but fails in Termux due to ELF format restrictions

   - projects/fl-blog/ARCHITECTURE.md:
     - System diagram showing GitHub Pages → Fetch API → Port 8253 backend
     - Three deployment scenarios (local, GitHub Pages + cloud, Vercel/Netlify)
     - CORS configuration details
     - Deployment checklist

   - projects/fl-blog/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md:
     - Complete setup instructions for all environments
     - Docker containerization example
     - PM2 process management for background execution
     - API endpoint specifications with response examples

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Go compilation issue: ELF format error ("unexpected e_type: 2") in Termux ARM environment
     - Fix: Switched to Node.js implementation (server.js) which runs successfully
     - User feedback: "오 이제 되네" (Oh, it works now)
   
   - Port 8253 EADDRINUSE error during testing:
     - Fix: Killed previous Node process before starting new test server
   
   - index.html string delimiter escaping error during Markdown-to-HTML conversion:
     - Original attempt: used backtick + quote concatenation causing syntax error
     - Fix: Changed to simple regex pattern using character class: "[#*`\\n]"
   
   - Port parsing in server.js: parseInt receiving ":8253" string
     - Fix: Added .replace(':', '') to strip leading colon from argument
   
   - CORS headers missing from initial server.js:
     - Fix: Added headers before request routing:
       ```javascript
       res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');
       res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'GET, POST, DELETE, OPTIONS');
       res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', 'Content-Type');
       ```

5. Problem Solving:
   - Initial Jekyll GitHub Pages setup failed with 404 errors on all routes
     - Solution: Abandoned Jekyll, created custom Node.js backend with static HTML frontend
   
   - Blog only served promotional purpose initially
     - Solution: Redesigned with dual-column layout and categorization to support both promotion AND technical verification
   
   - No comment functionality existed
     - Solution: Extended server-comments.js with full CRUD API, file-based persistence, search, and integrated UI
   
   - Go binary incompatible with Termux environment
     - Solution: Maintained both implementations but defaulted to Node.js for execution
   
   - Frontend needed to dynamically load and filter posts from backend
     - Solution: Implemented JavaScript with Fetch API, category assignment logic, and dynamic HTML generation

6. All user messages:
   - "깃허브 정적 홈페이지 253서버 백 엔드 이게 지시사항임" - GitHub static homepage + port 253 backend is the instruction
   - "실행" - Run (execution test request)
   - "블로그가 2가지 를 충족할거야 우리기술 외부흥보 2번은 기술 부족한거 체크하는 공식적인 보고라고 생각함" - Blog must satisfy 2 purposes: 1) External promotion of our technology, 2) Official report checking technology deficiencies
   - "댓글         │ ❌ 미구현 │ Disqus 통합  api 설계 글쓰기 댓글 검색 되게 가능?" - Comments not implemented - Disqus integration, API design, writing comments, comment search - is it possible?

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Deploy blog to actual GitHub Pages repository (index.html needs to be pushed to GitHub)
   - Deploy backend server to cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure/GCP) for production use
   - Optional: Integrate Disqus as backup/alternative comment system
   - Optional: Implement full-text search on posts (currently only comments are searchable)
   - Optional: Add RSS feed generation (/feed.xml endpoint)
   - Optional: Implement user authentication for comment moderation

8. Current Work:
   Just completed creation of server-comments.js with full comment system including:
   - POST /api/comments endpoint with validation for author/postSlug/text fields
   - JSON file persistence (comments.json)
   - GET /api/comments?postId={slug} for retrieving post comments sorted by date
   - DELETE /api/comments/{id} for removing comments
   - GET /api/search?q={query} for full-text comment search
   - Integrated comment UI in post detail page with form and comment list
   - Comment display with author name, date, text content, and delete link
   - Automatic page reload after comment submission/deletion
   - All endpoints return proper HTTP status codes and JSON responses

9. Optional Next Step:
   User's most recent explicit request was: "댓글         │ ❌ 미구현 │ Disqus 통합  api 설계 글쓰기 댓글 검색 되게 가능?" (Comments - API design, writing comments, comment search - is it possible?)

   The comment system has been fully implemented in server-comments.js. The next logical step would be to:
   - Test the comment system end-to-end by starting server-comments.js on port 8253 and verifying:
     1. POST /api/comments successfully creates and persists comments to comments.json
     2. GET /api/comments?postId=slug retrieves comments
     3. GET /api/search?q=keyword searches comments
     4. DELETE /api/comments/{id} removes comments
     5. POST /post/{slug} displays integrated comment form and list
   - However, this should be confirmed with the user first to ensure this is aligned with their priorities, as there are deployment and production considerations for the blog system.
